title: ECR: where the image lives before it runs

videos.script: Lesson 8 wrote a task definition that names an image. Lesson 9 ran it with no server underneath. Neither said where the image comes from. {{uri}} On AWS the usual answer is ECR, a registry inside your own account and region. Its address says whose it is and where it lives. {{push}} This lesson takes a push apart. A push is not one upload. It is a set of layers, and then a small file that lists them, called the manifest. The manifest's hash is the digest, and the digest is the image's real name. {{tags}} Tags are only pointers to that name, and pointers move. You will watch a tag move, see what it leaves behind, and lock it so it cannot. {{lifecycle}} Then a lifecycle policy, which deletes what nobody needs before the bill grows. {{scan}} And scanning, which finds known vulnerabilities in packages and says nothing about your code. moto answers ECR's API, but it is not a registry, so docker push has nowhere to go here. Each section says which part ran, and which part comes from AWS's documentation.
